strings: Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg is an Alliance bounty posted in Redridge Mountains targeting the warlord behind the Blackrock invasion of Stonewatch. Magistrate Solomon offers a generous reward for anyone daring enough to assault the conquered keep and bring back the commander's severed head.

Gath'Ilzogg is the brutal commander directing Blackrock clan raids across the Redridge Mountains. Under his direction, the orcs stormed and conquered Stonewatch Keep, turning a former human bastion into a fortified staging ground for assaults on the surrounding settlements. From the keep's highest ramparts, he plots further incursions into Lakeshire, threatening to cut Redridge off from the rest of the kingdom.
A Town Pushed to the Brink

With Stormwind's royal army failing to deploy reinforcements to the border regions, Magistrate Solomon has taken matters into his own hands. The township of Lakeshire simply lacks the military manpower to retake Stonewatch Keep by force. By posting a public bounty on Gath'Ilzogg, Solomon aims to decapitate the Blackrock leadership and spark the first stage of reclaiming the keep for the crown.

Gath'Ilzogg is an orc warlord leading the Blackrock clan forces occupying Stonewatch. He directed the conquest of the keep and is responsible for frequent deadly raids against the human settlers of Lakeshire.
gath'ilzogg lore | who is gathilzogg | blackrock leader redridge
He is entrenched at the very top of Stonewatch Keep, located in the eastern crags of the Redridge Mountains. He is heavily guarded by his Blackrock champions and bodyguards.
gath'ilzogg location | where is gathilzogg | stonewatch boss location
Why is Magistrate Solomon offering a bounty instead of sending soldiers?

Lakeshire's local town guard is stretched to the limit, and the crown in Stormwind has not sent the required troops to relieve the region. Magistrate Solomon has to rely on mercenaries and independent adventurers to handle major threats.
why a bounty | where are stormwind soldiers | lakeshire guard help
What happens after Gath'Ilzogg is killed?

Magistrate Solomon sees the warlord's death as the crucial first step toward clearing out the orc infestation and eventually reclaiming Stonewatch Keep for the Kingdom of Stormwind, though the Blackrock presence in the region remains heavy.
Why did the Blackrock orcs invade Stonewatch Keep?

The Blackrock clan uses Stonewatch Keep as a fortified forward base. Sitting high in the mountains above Redridge, it gives them strategic control over the passes and a direct launching point for raids against human settlements.
why are blackrock in redridge | why stonewatch taken
Who claims the bounty once Gath'Ilzogg is dead?
The bounty must be delivered directly to Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire's town hall, accompanied by Gath'Ilzogg's head as definitive proof of his defeat.
who to turn in gathilzogg | gathilzogg quest turn in
blackrock | bounty | gath'ilzogg | lakeshire | magistrate solomon | redridge | stonewatch | wanted poster
Breaching the summit of Stonewatch Keep means facing the hardened veteran warriors and brute strength of the Dark Horde's frontline command.
Striking down Gath'Ilzogg eliminates one of the most immediate military threats to the kingdom's eastern borders, buying vital breathing room for the citizens of Lakeshire.
For the people of Stormwind, Stonewatch Keep was a hard-won fortification; Gath'Ilzogg's slaughter of innocents during its fall makes this bounty a matter of bitter vengeance.
Why does Lakeshire want Gath'Ilzogg killed?

Gath'Ilzogg serves as the general directing the Blackrock orc invasion of Redridge. Under his command, the orcs slaughtered human defenders, captured Stonewatch Keep, and launched violent raids directly against the township of Lakeshire. Town leadership knows that so long as he coordinates their forces, the Blackrock clan will continue to plot atrocities against innocent citizens. Putting an end to him is critical to breaking the siege and eventually reclaiming the keep.
why kill gath'ilzogg | why gath'ilzogg bounty | why does solomon want gath'ilzogg dead
What is the Head of Gath'Ilzogg for?

The head provides indisputable proof that the Blackrock warlord has actually fallen. Magistrate Solomon needs concrete evidence of Gath'Ilzogg's demise before he can dispense the town's bounty and reassure the panicked citizens of Lakeshire that the architect behind the attacks has been dealt with.

Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle of the Gadgetzan Water Company says the Wastewander nomads now hold nearly every water well in the Tanaris desert. You are sent east of Gadgetzan to bring justice to the Wastewander Bandits and Thieves.

Out in the Tanaris desert, the Wastewander nomads now hold nearly every water well, and Gadgetzan's supply will soon run dry without access to them. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle, who has a taste for goblin-style justice, wants ten Wastewander Bandits and Thieves brought down east of town, and then a report back at once.

Bilgewhizzle is pleased with the speed of the work. The nomads are thinned enough that the company can start thinking about winning back its water wells, though it is far from done with the foul nomads and has more in mind.

You have done a good job so far, in Bilgewhizzle's view, but taking back the wells is best done against as few nomads as possible. Now the targets are the nomads' rogues, assassins and shadow mages, east and southeast of Gadgetzan. Bilgewhizzle admits they are a nasty lot, but says the wells are rightfully the company's.

The nomad population is now thin enough that the company can take the fight to them. Bilgewhizzle suggests speaking to Spigot Operator Luglunket in town, who gives a bounty on any Wastewander water pouches that came your way while dealing with the nomads.

In Darnassus, sacred ore is on its way to the forge. After you recover elunite from the shipwreck off Auberdine, Elanaria sends you to Mathiel to have it shaped into a weapon for the Kaldorei.

Elanaria sends you across Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace with the elunite ore you recovered from the haunted shipwreck off Auberdine. The warrior trainer packs it in a sturdy case and directs you to Mathiel, one of the capital's finest smiths. He can shape the metal into a weapon worthy of your calling.

Mathiel treats smithing as a craft of devotion. Elunite bears the sacred blessing of Elune, the Moon Goddess, and he accepts the case as an honor. He will shape the holy metal into arms to defend the young boughs of Teldrassil.
Mathiel is a skilled night elf blacksmith who works in Darnassus's Warrior's Terrace. He makes specialty arms and accepts custom work for the city's defenders.

In Darnassus, Weapons of Elunite brings a young warrior's early rite of passage to its close. After recovering ore blessed by Elune, you bring it to Mathiel to forge arms for a defender of Kalimdor.

Night elf warriors defend Teldrassil and the kaldorei people. Promising young warriors gather elunite, a mineral blessed by the Moon Goddess, rather than relying on mundane steel alone. Its ore calls for a smith skilled in metalcraft and mindful of Elune's gift.

Smith Mathiel works in Darnassus, shaping blessed elunite into weapons of war. He considers the work an honor, not routine metalcraft. When you bring him the ore, he fashions arms to suit your style and rewards your service with weapons blessed by your goddess.

This rite of passage for a young warrior in Darnassus reaches its end when you bring elunite ore to Smith Mathiel. He forges weapons blessed by Elune to aid your journey across Kalimdor.

Sentries and temple guards are sworn to defend Darnassus and Teldrassil from active threats, leaving them no leisure to gather rare smithing materials for personal armaments. By undertaking the labor to gather the ore yourself, you prove your dedication and discipline, earning a weapon forged specifically to match your martial path.

At the Lakeshire Inn, Yorus Barleybrew awaits Alliance warriors bold enough to answer his challenge. Trainers across Alliance capitals send seasoned fighters from Stormwind toward the Redridge borderlands to meet the eccentric dwarf and face his test of arms.

Across Alliance capitals, warrior trainers watch fighters who have outgrown their first drills. When an apprentice proves their mettle around their twentieth season, trainers such as Kelv Sternhammer, Wu Shen, and Darnath Bladesinger pass along word of Yorus Barleybrew. The dwarf offers no standard military order. Instead, he has issued an open wager and a test of arms to any Alliance warrior bold enough to answer.

Yorus Barleybrew waits at the tavern in Lakeshire, on the front lines of Redridge's struggle against encroaching gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Those who find him meet a boastful dwarf with a hearty drink in hand, ready to judge any challenger who claims true fighting spirit. For warriors seeking to prove themselves beyond the capital's safe cobbled streets, his trial opens onto the harsher battles of the frontier.

Yorus Barleybrew is a dwarf of the famous Barleybrew brewing clan who has issued an open martial challenge to Alliance warriors. He waits at the Lakeshire Inn, where he tests fighters who believe they are ready for the brutal frontier of Redridge Mountains.

As an Alliance recruit, you may be sent to Lakeshire, a vulnerable settlement beset by gnolls and Blackrock orcs.
Why are the trainers sending you to Yorus Barleybrew?

Your trainers recognize that you have outgrown basic drills and require trials that test your mettle in the field. Yorus Barleybrew issued an open challenge specifically to able Alliance warriors, promising a grand reward to anyone strong enough to overcome it. The Rethban Gauntlet is an eccentric endurance trial devised by the dwarven brewer Yorus Barleybrew in Lakeshire. Challengers must drink a potent swig of his family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder and sprint north into the gnoll-infested Rethban Caverns and back before an hour elapses.

In the town of Lakeshire, where grim talk of gnoll raids and missing town guards usually dominates the inn, the dwarf Yorus Barleybrew brings a distinctly dwarven flavor of entertainment. His self-styled challenge, the Rethban Gauntlet, tests an adventurer's mettle, speed, and liver all at once. Participants are required to down a draught of his family's signature concoction, Barleybrew Scalder, right before setting off on foot toward the northern foothills.

The trial is far more perilous than a simple drunken footrace. Between Lakeshire and the destination lies Redridge territory teeming with aggressive Redridge gnolls. To successfully complete the gauntlet, the runner must fight or slip past the packs, reach the first fork inside the dark tunnels of Rethban Caverns, and hustle back to Yorus within an hour—all while battling the overwhelming, staggering effects of the fiery dwarven alcohol.
Yorus Barleybrew, a dwarven brewer staying in Lakeshire, challenges travelers to the run to prove their fortitude and test his brew.
who gives rethban gauntlet | yorus barleybrew quest | who starts the gauntlet
What makes this challenge particularly difficult?

Aside from navigating the gnoll packs roaming the Redridge foothills within a strict one-hour time limit, runners must first swallow Barleybrew Scalder, an intense beverage that leaves them severely intoxicated and struggling to maintain their balance.
why is rethban gauntlet hard | barleybrew scalder effect

The caverns sit in the northern foothills of Redridge Mountains, northwest of Lakeshire. The path leads north past local homesteads toward the crags inhabited by gnoll packs.

Surviving the gauntlet proves your endurance to Yorus Barleybrew, opening the way to further tasks in the region such as seeking out the shieldsmith Furen Longbeard in Stormwind.

While Lakeshire struggles under the threat of gnoll incursions, braving the gauntlet helps thin out enemy patrols prowling near the northern caves.
Dwarves will feel right at home with Yorus's boisterous concept of fun: mixing potent family liquor with dangerous mountain sprints.
Why does Yorus Barleybrew want this done?

Yorus Barleybrew is not looking to solve a crisis or save Lakeshire with this trial. Instead, he devises the Rethban Gauntlet as a boisterous test of nerve, endurance, and alcohol tolerance. By sending daring adventurers deep into gnoll territory while thoroughly intoxicated on his family's fiery Barleybrew Scalder, Yorus seeks pure entertainment and the thrill of watching someone brave enough to conquer both Redridge's savage gnolls and his brew's staggering kick.

Balir Frosthammer calls for help as troggs surge through Coldridge Valley. Rockjaw troggs are breaking through across Dun Morogh, catching dwarven mountaineers off guard and threatening the settlements and camps.

In Coldridge Valley, Rockjaw troggs are clawing up from below in growing numbers. Anvilmar hears reports of them swarming the frozen lake and nearby foothills. Their attacks disrupt patrols and cut off supply routes through the valley pass, turning a training refuge for young dwarven warriors and mountaineers into a place under threat.

A dwarven camp west of the valley has fallen to a coordinated trogg attack. The mountaineers retreated and abandoned their posts. Ironforge cannot spare full battle regiments, so Balir Frosthammer calls on newly recruited adventurers to fight through the Rockjaw ranks and secure the hills before the creatures reach Anvilmar.
Balir Frosthammer is a seasoned dwarven mountaineer stationed outside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He organizes defenses against wild beasts and troggs threatening local recruits.

Rockjaw troggs are tunneling up from deep fissures across Dun Morogh. Coldridge Valley is among the first populated valleys struck as the creatures break through and overrun surface camps.

As a young Bronzebeard dwarf leaving Anvilmar, you have a personal duty to drive back the troggs and protect Dun Morogh's sacred grounds and tunnels.

Coldridge Valley is under immediate siege. The troggs have not only infested the southern hills and the frozen lake, but just nights ago they violently overran the dwarven camp to the west. Balir needs their numbers thinned before the savage creatures push deeper into the valley and overwhelm Anvilmar entirely.

The defenders at Anvilmar are dangerously shorthanded. The recent surprise attack on their western camp scattered their forces and left the garrison stretched thin trying to hold the settlement's perimeter. With no surplus soldiers to spare for an offensive counterattack, Balir must recruit any able-bodied adventurer who arrives.

Following the creation of specialized armor, the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard sends a copy of his findings across the district to Grimand Elmore. The brief errand carries technical notes between two headstrong weaponsmiths sharing space in Stormwind City.

Having forged the specialized Fire Hardened Mail, Furen Longbeard documents the intricate heat-treating techniques and elemental principles he uncovered during the process. Rather than keeping the knowledge entirely to himself, he commits the notes to parchment and tasks an adventurer with delivering them straight to Grimand Elmore, a seasoned crafter operating out of a nearby weapon shop.

Grimand Elmore's immediate reaction upon receiving the manuscript is wounded pride. Adamant that he taught Furen everything the younger dwarf knows, Grimand bristles at the notion that his former pupil could offer him instruction. Despite his outward indignation, the craftsman cannot resist perusing the text, quickly finding an intriguing idea hidden within the notes that he is eager to test for himself.

Grimand Elmore is a respected weaponsmith who maintains a shop in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. He is known for his immense professional pride and his past role in teaching craft skills to other local smiths, including Furen Longbeard.
grimand elmore | who is grimand | elmore stormwind
Why does Furen send notes to Grimand?

While crafting the Fire Hardened Mail, Furen discovered new techniques and recorded his methods. He wanted to share the breakthroughs with Grimand, even while knowing Grimand's fiery temper and stubborn ego would make him react defensively to being taught something new.
why send notes | furen notes | furen to grimand
Where can Grimand Elmore be found?
He can be found working inside the weapon shop located within the Dwarven District of Stormwind City, only a short walk from Furen Longbeard's forge.
where is grimand | grimand location | grimand elmore shop
How does Grimand react to the notes?

Grimand is initially outraged, declaring that he taught Furen everything the dwarf knows. However, his curiosity as a master smith quickly takes over when he spots an intriguing technique in the text that he wants to experiment with.
What happens after Grimand reads the notes?
Intrigued by Furen's work on fire-tempering metal, Grimand decides to pursue his own ambitious craft project, which leads into further tasks to gather rare components with elemental heat.

The exchange between Furen and Grimand illustrates the intense professional rivalry and sharing of trade secrets common among master metalworkers.
The hot-headed, prideful banter between Grimand and Furen reflects the deeply competitive yet cooperative traditions of Khaz Modan's smithing culture.
Why does Furen send you instead of going to Grimand himself?

Furen knows Grimand Elmore's prickly temper all too well. Grimand claims to have taught Furen everything he knows, and having his former student stroll into his shop to lecture him on new smithing techniques would ignite a fiery row. By having you deliver the notes instead, Furen avoids a direct confrontation and lets his stubborn mentor swallow his pride in private.

In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard has a new armor design for an Alliance warrior. The dwarf armorer offers to forge Fire Hardened Mail if the warrior brings him rare materials from both continents.

Furen Longbeard has forged an exceptional buckler for the aspiring warrior and now proposes a greater work: mail made to withstand fierce blows. His craft calls for more than iron or steel. He needs rare materials touched by elemental heat and natural resilience. Furen cannot leave his Stormwind forge, so the warrior seeking the armor must gather these dangerous ingredients.

Furen sends the warrior to distant wilds and dangerous depths for the parts he needs. The recipe calls for fangs from venomous spiders in the damp crevices of the Wetlands, along with scorched and galvanized horns from fierce chimaeras in the Stonetalon Mountains. To bind and temper those beast parts into mail, Furen also needs volatile phlogiston from Roogug, a geomancer deep within Razorfen Kraul's thorny maze in the Barrens.
Furen Longbeard is a veteran dwarf armorer and shieldsmith in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. He crafts tailored defenses for promising warriors willing to help him.
furen | who gives fire hardened mail | who is the smith
Why does Furen require such strange ingredients?

Furen needs unusual ingredients to temper the metal beyond ordinary dwarven methods. His secret craft uses organic materials conditioned by natural venom, mountain winds, and breath weapons, together with volatile phlogiston.

As an Alliance soldier, you venture deep into the Barrens and Stonetalon Mountains, where the Horde contests the land.
As a dwarf, you know true armor calls for unyielding materials taken straight from nature's harshest predators.
Why does Furen Longbeard want this done?

Furen takes fierce pride in his smithcraft. Having already crafted your shield, he wants to prove his mastery by forging an exceptionally tough suit of mail. He knows the secret techniques required to work these exotic, fire-tempered reagents, and he offers to craft the mail for you simply to see such extraordinary armor brought into being—provided you are willing to brave the perils of gathering the components.

In Stormwind, Yorus Barleybrew sends warriors back after a harrowing trial in the Redridge Mountains. He gives them a cask of Barleybrew Scalder to take to Furen Longbeard, who will fashion a stout shield.

After you prove your mettle against the gnolls and perils of the Rethban Gauntlet, Yorus Barleybrew honors his bargain. The promised reward cannot be hammered out in Lakeshire, so he directs promising fighters back to Stormwind City. A dwarven armorer there stands ready to repay a personal debt.

Yorus gives you a heavy cask of Barleybrew Scalder instead of a letter of credit. Take it to Furen Longbeard in Stormwind's Dwarven District, where soot and hammer-clatter fill the air. The seasoned smith recognizes the name behind the delivery and lends his craft to a warrior seeking a stout shield.
